## Update build-tools image references to latest master version

We need to update the build-tools container image references used in this repository to point to the latest master version. The build-tools image is the standard development environment for Istio projects, and keeping it current ensures we have the latest tooling, dependencies, and fixes.

The references that need updating are:
- The image tag in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (used for development container environments)
- The `IMAGE_VERSION` default value in `common/scripts/setup_env.sh` (used when resolving the build container)

Additionally, the `common/.commonfiles.sha` file records the commit hash of the istio/common-files repository that these shared scripts and configurations were synced from — this needs to be updated to reflect the newer version we're pulling in.

The goal is to bring all three files in sync with the current `istio/common-files@master` state. Please update these to match the latest build-tools image tag (which follows the pattern `master-<commit-sha>`).

## Environment Setup
Check `Makefile.core.mk` and `common/Makefile.common.mk` for how common files are synchronized (look for targets related to "update-common"). The `common/.commonfiles.sha` file tracks the source version. For general project build/test setup, refer to `Makefile` and `Makefile.core.mk`.

## Implementation Plan
1. Identify the latest build-tools image tag from the istio build-tools repository (typically in the form `master-<40-char-commit-sha>`).
    2. Update the `"image"` field in `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` to use the new tag.
    3. Update the default `IMAGE_VERSION` value in `common/scripts/setup_env.sh` to match the new tag.
    4. Determine the current commit SHA from istio/common-files@master that corresponds to the build-tools version being used.
    5. Update `common/.commonfiles.sha` to this new SHA.
    6. Optionally run any "update-common" make target (if available) to ensure all other common files are synchronized, but limit changes to only what's necessary.

  if [[ -f "$1" ]]; then
    local local_config
